objective: Determine whether the surviving 5x3-k3 MOD2_P_TACTICAL2 value collisions are component-algebra failures or aliases created by retaining only turn parity while discarding admissible current-rank phase.

trigger.observed_rank_effect: the paired substitution changes total rank by 2 while preserving turn parity

frozen_from_prior: T2 evaluator short circuit: W immediate win, L2 universal one-move release loss, O unresolved
exact value labels remain downstream qualification targets only

candidate_distinctions.definition: append exact current rank to MOD2 component parity + T2
candidate_distinctions.role: admissible upper-bound test for rank-phase aliasing

candidate_distinctions.definition: append current rank modulo 3 while retaining existing turn parity p
candidate_distinctions.role: smaller candidate suggested by prior MOD3 multiplicity QV success
nearby falsification control; must not be promoted merely for being small

candidate_distinctions.definition: exact rank + MOD2 component parity without T2
candidate_distinctions.role: tests whether rank alone explains the earlier failures

anti_circularity: No component type or tactical rule is changed after observing values.
Rank is a governing-objective admissible current-rank fact, not an outcome-derived feature.
The fresh 3x6-k3 carrier does not contribute to candidate definition.
All structural keys are frozen before exact values are derived.
falsifiers: Any same-exact-rank mixed-value group under MOD2+T2 rejects pure rank-phase aliasing as a complete explanation in that case.
Any fresh RANK_EXACT mixed-value group rejects exact-rank-conditioned MOD2+T2 QV sufficiency on that holdout.
RANK_MOD3 failure with RANK_EXACT success shows the six-phase compression is too small.
RANK_EXACT_NO_T2 failure shows rank is complementary to, not a replacement for, tactical reduction.
nonclaims: A finite pass does not prove standard-7x6 sufficiency.
A rank-conditioned pass does not prove literal Nim heaps or universal XOR.
MOD3 multiplicity success is not interpreted as a ternary algebra unless phase-preservation alternatives are excluded.
